_note: Campaign VI - SOFT MATTER. 10 HD plates, avg 9.45. Bone, chalk, blush. The jewellery is the only hard object present and it is physically changing the soft thing around it; every event leaves a record you can read. Internally: the easiest set to layer type onto - every frame is bone, chalk or blush with an untouched two-fifths, built for anything where the copy has to lead.

frames.shows: A pearl strand floating a pearl's width above sifted chalk, with a shallow dish printed in the powder for every single pearl. One strand, one toggle, one drop.
A blush stain spreading outward from under each earring on damp blotting paper. Five petals, a pave halo round the oval stone, small stones scattered on the petals.
The ring rolled on its side across soft chalk so its granulation prints a track of thousands of dots, like a printing block.
Half buried in a chalk drift with the wavy ring and both pearls left in the clear.
Tissue torn under the earrings' own weight, one crescent per earring in the exact curve of its outer edge.
The pearl half dusted matte and almost gone; the gold sphere mirror-bright with a clean crater cleared around it.
The chain lying down inside a channel cut in blush wax, the empty groove running on ahead with a link-shaped impression for every link.
Coiled in crushed blush crepe whose creases radiate outward from it. Top two-fifths kept flat; the tag is blank.
Standing head-first in soft chalk, sunk to exactly its own depth, a scatter of loose pink powder round the rim.
Every fold in the linen radiating from the charm. Four rounded lobes with a round stone in each and a gold bead at the centre.
